name: John
overview: John is a male biblical figure uniquely identified as the father of Peter and Andrew. No tribal affiliation or additional notes are provided about him. His role is primarily recognized through his paternal relationship to these significant disciples.
namesAndTitles: The name John means 'y-h-v-h is gracious,' reflecting a common Hebrew theophoric name. There is only one recorded name for him, and it does not appear to have been given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records John as the father of Simon (Peter) and Andrew, establishing his family connection to two of Jesus' prominent disciples. No other family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: John's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his role as the father of Peter and Andrew, who were key followers of Christ. His familial connection places him at the foundation of the early apostolic community, linking him to the beginnings of the church through his sons. This relationship highlights the human context behind the calling of Jesus' disciples.
